chunks: Several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from several, from Abu Jameela, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Give charity, even if it is with a Sa' of dates, or even with part of a Sa', or even with a handful, or even with part of a handful, or even with one date, or even with half a date. So whoever cannot find (even that), let him give with soft words.'

For indeed, one of you will meet Allah, and it will be said to him: 'Did I not do (such and such) with you? Did I not make you hearing and seeing? Did I not make for you wealth and children?' So he will say, 'Yes.' Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will say: 'So look what you have sent ahead for yourself.'
He said: 'So he will look in front of him, and behind him, and to his right, and to his left, and he will not find anything with which he can shield his face from the Fire.'

key_terms.صَاع: A unit of volume measurement, approximately 3 liters.

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of charity one should give according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the Shia emphasis on the accessibility of charity, affirming that even the poorest can fulfill this obligation through 'soft words' (kalimat layyinah) if material means are absent. It highlights the eschatological accountability for divine blessings (sami‘, basir, mal, walad), warning that neglecting charity leaves one defenseless against the Hellfire, a theme resonating with the concept of *hissab* (accounting) in Shia theology.
